reviews.review: Amazing game! A lot bigger than I expected. I finished the story and still have lots of stuff to go back for. The eldritch horror is definitely the best part of the game imo. Great atmosphere. Good controls and combat.
I love this game. It hast a fast paced movement with shooting, magic and melee mechanics. It was one of those games, and there are litte for me, wich I have finished and restarted immediately.

I like it. It's hard to imagine, but think of The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past meets Bloodborne's horror in a wild west setting. It's a love letter to each, and I find this game is wonderful. Some enemies and bosses can be difficult at times, but given the right tools, weapons, and patience, fights are challenging yet fair. Knowing where to go at times can be a struggle, and I'll note I've had to resort to the dev's own guide for help. Overall I do recommend this game, and I hope it gets a sequel or spinoff someday.

Really good. 2D Zelda meets 2D Bloodborne set in a western. Controls are responsive and snappy. Combat is just hard enough to be satisfying. I like the mix of sword and gun combat. Could use a better map and I found myself unsure where to go next a lot. But overall very fun.
I have not played a game this fun in ages!
didnt expect it to be this big. combat is smooth and feels really nice. overall just a good game

The game stutters terribly for me when the screen scrolls, which is near constantly. It's bad enough that it induces nausea. I can't find any forum posts that report similar behavior. 

Worse when running full screen, but happens even when running windowed. There are almost no in-game display settings to tinker with, so there's no way to troubleshoot. Shame, it seemed like a fun game otherwise.

intel i9-10900K
64GB RAM
NVidia RTX 3080
reviews.developer_response: Hi, thanks for playing and for the note on your experience. There shouldn't be stuttering - and your specs are more than adequate. Can you contact us to see how we can troubleshoot? You can contact info@midwestgames.com or in our Discord at https://discord.gg/dJjb5PJThz.

reviews.review:
game is fun. but fucking hell some silly decisions. feel free to read the novel below
<5 mins into the game, you're forced to choose between 1 of ~10 classes. Each class has a specialty among the ~8? stats listed. None of these stats are explicitly defined, you're locked into the class you choose, with 0 flexibility. From that point, you may level only 3 of these stats, HP, Stamina, Madness resistance. The reason I'm not even sure how many stats are presented at the class selection screen is that you can't even view what your other stats are. They show up, unexplained, force you into a class, and then disappear, hope you chose right with literally 0 information. 

tldr: the game asks you to lock in to a play style within <5 mins and provides literally no flexibility later. i.e. if you chose occultist, you best be castin spells bc your melee damage is 50% the soldier class lmao
AMAZING GAME!!!! 10/10
Этой игре кровь из носа нужна нормальная карта( с проходами и хоть какой-то структурой уровня), а то, что есть можно один раз открыть, полюбоваться и больше никогда не открывать

Best game I've played in a while, great combat and story. Interesting atmosphere and cool characters. I was looking to itch that classic puzzle game, like the isometric legend of zelda experience, and i found that with Ocean Hearts: the previous game by this developer I think. I finished Ocean Heart's in a haste, and I was lucky to see that Tombwater had just released. Imagine my glee when I find out it's an unfamiliar but fresh arpg with fast paced combat to match it's grit. Couldn't put down
Very cool take on the genres.
Great game. Top tier metroidvania soulslike with a western meets bloodborne aesthetic.

very very fun game. I love that it has a demo; that's all it took to hook me.. It has been very fun playing it right at release, because there's like 0 guides out there for me to ruin the discovery. lol

My only gripe is that you cannot use melee weapons diagonally. You can shoot in all directions fine, but somehow melee combat is awkward if you've played similar games before. Enemies can attack in every direction but you can't and I understand why this would put people off. 
Regardless, I kept going and 100%'d it in 2 playthroughs. They nailed the spooky western town atmosphere with its visuals and sound design. It almost felt like playing Blood West in 2D with Hyper Light Drifter gameplay.
Anyone who's into challenging combat and LOTS of exploration should give this game a go.
There's no way I can't leave a good review. As a sucker for wild west things this was so much fun. If you like pixel style adventure games like I do this is a must

It's top down, it's Wild West, it's metroidvania, it has eldritch horrors, it has a bit of unconventional combat, it has some rather showboat-ey spells with a lot of flair, it has a fairly intriguing story, it's punishing, it's a nice, small, niche game, what more do I need?
its a good game get it :p

A or S tier Metroidvania with a very cool world to explore, a very unique perspective in this genre (blending Soulslike and Zeldalike conventions in a Metroidvania format--with cowboys!), varied enemies and strong combat. The best part is that exploration is very incentivized and rewarded.

This game is super fun and I love the 
spookies.
the boss transformations are suprizing and gun is fun and intuitive to use
Super fun game fans of Soulslikes will instantly enjoy. Works perfectly on steam deck.

So this is an interesting game. Its a soulslike with a western meets bloodborne theme. And it works well. It is not perfect. Its pretty easy to lose your place in the world due to the map being very basic. Also melee attacks only attack in 4 directions and this causes problems when fighting some of the tougher fights. I think this game very much needs a lock on. Also, while I like the atmosphere, I feel way more could have been done with it. Its pretty basic stuff for the most part if you played any western games. All that said, everything is still very solid and fun. Exploration has that soulslike cadence and it feels good here. There are a bunch of weapons and spells to mess with, although apart from one or two spells I found them pretty harmless to the enemies. And the story while kinda simple is still interesting and good. Good job dev or devs. I give the game a 7.75 out of 10.
I am only 5 hours in and I am blown away by how fun the combat and exploring is. If you like Zelda, souls likes, isometric view, blood borne. This game is for you. No hand holding tho so go explore!

This game is VERY good. If you like the sound of A Link to the Past + Bloodborne set in the Wild West, you will like this game. The standard difficulty is very difficult but thankfully they added difficulty sliders for the less hardcore players like me. They did a great job creating an immersive experience with tons of different interesting biomes, weapons and RPG stat upgrades. The pixel art is top notch as well. Definitely recommended.

It's a Zelda/Metroidvania with Souls-like aspects.
While I wouldn't say its as hard as some Souls-like it does have difficulty on normal settings....However....GOOD NEWS EVERYBODY...you will be traveling to the West with a damage taken slider you can tone down as much as you want!

If you are fan of Old School Zelda, Metroidvanias I wouldn't miss this one. 9/10 so far; long ways to go yet but I am hooked.

The game is amazing. It has that great souls like combat and world exploration with interconnected locations. One things I'd like to recommend to those who begin playing it. MARK YOUR MAP. the map given is a simple basic map design and I find it cool that you can mark it all over to let you keep track of things in the world. 

I did not begin doing it until much after leaving the first town area. I just wanted to make sure to suggest that to any new players who might come across this review.

Tombwater is a Pixel art Souls-like that mixes the Eldritch horror of Bloodborne with a western aesthetic. Bullets for your guns are charged via melee combat, encouraging mixing your approach against the wide variety of enemies across the cursed town of Tombwater and the surrounding wilderness. 

The game offer a great variety of weapons, guns, explosives and spells, meaning it offers all manner of different playstyles with their own strengths an weaknesses (Although like most souls likes Spells are SUPER POWERFUL). You start off picking a class that often have unique weapons or tools for their playthrough. 

There are some issues, I missed out on an NPC Questline due to a bug at the start of the game, their is a tinnitus like sound when you take massive damage that drove me nuts and I found a couple of times that dashing was a little finicky, but aside from that I had an absolute blast. 

If you are looking for a fun, engaging game with a good amount of challenge and fun secrets, I recommend picking up Tombwater.
Link to the Past + Bloodborne + Red Dead Redemption 2 = Tombwater. Highly recommended. The only downsides are the controls take some getting used to and the map is atrocious, practically worthless.

Having seen the credits, but still missing out on some end game content, I definitely know that I played enough of the game to recommend it to others.  There was a lot of love put into this game, and it shows in every aspect of it.  There are certain design choices that might turn off certain players, so keep that in mind before taking the plunge into madness.  

The map seems to be the most hot button issue with the game since you only get to see a general layout of the world, but it doesn't apply to indoor areas.  You can put an assortment of markers on it, but they are typically not super helpful.  I will probably never 100% the game due to this, and tbh, I don't 100% many games, but this one seems like it'd be a chore.  However, the way locations are laid out and the generous amount of shortcuts are very much appreciated. 

The bosses are really interesting and most of them are quite different from one another.  There are always save points near the toughest ones, and typically a shortcut to them as well.  You have tons of different weapons, spells, and guns to pick from, so whatever on your preferences, you will find something that works for you.  I see a lot of people complain that you can only do melee attacks in the cardinal directions, but I never thought this was a problem.  Some of the spells are a bit too OP, but I chose to rarely use them.  I also need to mention that this has the typical soulslike BS where when you die, you drop your loot and have to go get it from your dead body.  I pretty much hate this mechanic, but I never lost my currency in my playthrough so it isn't too hard to get it back.  (You get a lot of health flasks).

The worldbuilding is fantastic throughout the whole game.  There are many instances of dialogue, but it never felt like it took away from the pace the game sets from the beginning.  You will run into little areas where you can relive a memory from the town that paint in the details in a creative way.  I have never been into narratives in games, but I can tell that this one is better than most.  

All in all, I had a great time with the game so far and I will eventually find the bosses that I missed and defeat them.  The devs put out a really good walkthrough in the community hub, and I had to use it once so far to find something I was missing.  I am sure I will use it again, so I am really glad it is there.  If you are into top-down action games that fall on the difficult side of things, that have a huge area to explore, and that are immersive from start to finish, then you should really check this one out!

This is a great game. Its basically Hyper Light Cowboy Drifter. 

Great bosses, a very interconnected exploration focused world, easy to get lost in. If you like a game where you start off weak and turn into a juggernaut at the end, this is definitely one of those.

My only two criticisms are that the soundtrack had no memorable great tracks and you almost become too overpowered at the end to the point where i was just destroying bosses without paying too much attention to mechanics.

I definitely think this is worth picking up. The game is a Frankenstein amalgamation of 2d Zelda games, Bloodborne, and Western clichés in the best possible way. The whole game felt like a labor of love.

There are tons of weapons, guns, spells, consumables, trinkets, upgrade options, enemy types, NPCs questlines, and secret areas to find. I was engaged for my whole playthrough.

I'll admit that my early game impressions were "WTH where am I?" and "why the frak do these enemies attack so fast???"

I don't mean either of those things negatively, though. Early game really feels like a 2D Bloodborne.

Tombwater gives you so many tools / pathways to power up that late game you'll likely find it too easy if you explore thoroughly. I found that rewarding... though I would have liked some of the late game bosses to be a bit beefier. (The game has damage applied / received sliders that can be decreased or increased, if you want to tune it to your specifications. I played through on the default settings.)

Placing map markers to navigate and identify "come back later" POIs was a fun (and necessary) minigame. I usually complain about AAA games *not* doing this, so I found it a welcome addition here. As other reviews have said, the map itself is imperfect, and there are times when you are underground where it is difficult to accurately place markers. It didn't impact my enjoyment of the game, though.

The cartoony Western-themed Zelda graphics trying to be Bloodborne-style cosmic horror don't always click, and the sound design is either forlorn or playful, but not especially spooky. Despite that, the game is gorgeous and I found the soundtrack enjoyable.

Some spells are egregiously op, and *some* weapons / guns feel underpowered. I don't know if a balance pass is in the cards, and honestly it's in a pretty good state as is. I'd still suggest giving it a... shot. My playtime was for a run with 82% of achievements.
Hate but fair game that doesn't hold the players hand.

I can't get enough of this game. I'm posting a review to help the cause so it can be successful so they can release a DLC. I need more content of this ASAP. 

The combat and movement feels amazing, there is tons of variability in builds, weapons, lots of secrets to uncover, I love the atmosphere, the world and art is beautiful. Just stunning game all around, Moth Atlas cooked so hard.

The only downside I will say is the map is useless. I laughed when I zoomed in, it's really only good when zoomed out so you have a general sense of where an area is.
Rootin' tootin' Bloodborne, it just works.

Phenomenal game! 
Wonderfully designed world filled with secrets!

A very good game with surprising depth. Exploration is rewarding and mostly fun, bogged down slightly by a bad map. A notable variety of build possibilities exist, with many weapons and spells tuned to be strong enough to use into the end game. Difficult, but not over-tuned. Highly recommend!

A really well done game! It mixes visual and story themes of Western and Eldritch stories with a big explorable world and souls-like combat in a *really* good way! Some bosses feel *little* nasty sometimes, but nothing that can't be overcome.

What a fantastic horror themed souls-like in a weird west setting! Strongly recommended! Excellent atmosphere and sound / music design with cozy but challenging gameplay.

I cannot express how much I love this game. It is probably the best souls like I have played since Bloodborne. The overall tone and atmosphere are top notch despite obvious graphical limitations. The music... oh my god, the music goes so hard!
Its like if Bloodborne was a Western
very nice game! zelda + bloodborne

I like it, but I wouldn't recommend it. It's missing an x-factor.

+ Spooky ambient soundtrack with guitar licks. Yeehaw!
+ Every player has access to weapons, guns, renewing craftables, spells, and weapon arts... No stat requirements!
+ Robust character customization from all the above [i]and[/i] a Hollow Knight-inspired badge system
+ Surprising amount of speaking characters with coherent questlines
+ Nice variety of level themes

/ This might be the first Soulslike where I found more spells than weapons
/ You can only attack in 4 directions, and enemies are frequently knocked back at a diagonal. It adds a wrinkle (do you follow up with gunfire or retreat?) but I'd prefer to attack in 360°
/ Areas connect in all directions, but most shortcuts aren't useful or have weak contextualization. Exploration is open-ended but to the point of incoherence

- Areas are small, so navigation isn't [i]difficult[/i], per-se, but individual rooms are frumpy and unmemorable—it's difficult to form a mental map
- Obstacles requiring upgrades aren't marked, but there are map markers...! But if those obstacles are indoors or below-ground, that doesn't get a separate map... You can stand [i]directly on top of your own map marker[/i] and be in the wrong place
- You can't level individual offensive stats despite how they're displayed at class selection... If you start as an Occultist, you'll always deal 50% less melee damage than a Soldier, with no way to pivot
- Tons of dud weapons. Awkward ranges, unfortunate hitstun thresholds, and for some reason only 1/3 of em have Weapon Arts
- It's easy to rush-down large enemies and bosses by dumping all your combat resources into them at once. Spam is king
- Conspicuous lack of sound including: ambiance, large enemy footsteps, Bloodborne villager-esque chatter, large monster breathing, etc
- Game lacks personality, somehow? There aren't monsters so grotesque or strange that I'm like, "Never seen that before!" 

The negatives don't directly outweigh the positives, but the game's highs aren't that high, so all the little frustrations fail to become likable little quirks in service of something greater, and it ends up underwhelming.

This game has ruled the last 4 hours of my life. While it's low res, it's highly charming and also somewhat unsettling in some portions. The difficulty isn't through the roof and I'm constantly rewarded for exploring the locations it has. If I had one significant criticism, it would be that the map is not particularly easy to understand when trying to get to new locations or relocate locations that you were locked out of earlier. 

The team does a good job of keeping hints regarding where you need to go next, but it certainly doesn't hold your hand. Surprisingly, that's actually a good thing because it gives you more time to grind and grow your character. Thanks for the plethora of tools that they provide for you. There's many different methods to solve challenging fights. 

If I had to pick some games this reminds me of I would probably pick Hyper Light Drifter and maybe Bastion. Regardless, I can't wait to spend more time with this game, especially on my steam deck.

Excelente juego, con una buena historia, buena jugabilidad, buenas peleas, un buen conjunto de armas, poderes e items para armarte a gusto. Tiene buenas horas de duración, para darle un buen vicio. Ojalá algún día lo traduzcan al español.

Can I do a sideways thumb? The game sacrifices the authenticity of the west for liberal 'rule of cool' application, which is occasionally distracting but never truly unwelcome. I also want to shout out the ost/sound design - there's a lot of confidence in the 'less is more' that I really appreciate! 

But that map sucks. Getting around is a nightmare, and while I don't mind backtracking there's no areas that are actively fun to backtrack through. The areas in the first 2/3rds of the game all bleed together so I don't feel any motivation to go back and see what I missed - the amount of times I was like 'oh I remember seeing something like this but i have no idea where and I don't care to try' was astronomical. This had the side effect of not knowing where to go for plot reasons, which [i]then[/i] had the side effect of being supremely overleveled for the last stretch of the game. - I think I just facetanked the last few bosses and it was fine. All that frustration makes it a tough recc, but when the game is confident it does cool stuff. Get it on sale, I guess?

A very nice game all together. Highlights for me are: The art and music which build the weird west very well. Controls are fluid and responsive which for a souls like is always a must but not always is what you get. Bosses are a lot of fun and many of them will force you to use the games mechanics to bet them. The setting and the idea as a whole are a breath of fresh air and I would definitely like to see more from the devs and hope they will want to add more content like a DLC or maybe a continuation? :) Now the game was not perfect and had some issues but overall I'd say these were minor, sometimes it would be easy to just get lost and be stuck for a longer time (for me it was the mining camp as my smoothbrain couldn't figure out that you can shoot the lever to move to a different part of the map xD). No critical hit animation was a bit of a missed opportunity and only having the stun-shove was nice but not enough especially in elite or boss encounters. Also a thing to improve on in my eyes would be enemy movesets, I'd say the common enemies or in some cases elite ones could have an extra move to mix things up and also I'd say most of the enemies could have more of chase down options to make it more challenging. All in all I'd say this is a solid 7/10 as it was fun to play and discover the story.

Finished it! Here is my  comprehensive review:

LIKE CASTING DYNAMITE?

You like Ew icky?

You like the Zelda?

YOU LIKE COWDOYS?!

Geet it. . small dev team. 

Tons of builds, cool system for classes (you pick a class, all weapons and spells and useable items are available)

Twists and turns get a bit tough with the map system 

BUT the juice is worth the squeeze.  Support the little guys. 

Buckit approved.

Tombwater is a phenomenal 2d metroidvania that does everything right. The thing that really made me love this game is how fun the combat is. It's fast-paced and engaging, and there are a massive amount of spells, weapons, and gadgets, many of which are unique or strange to encourage experimentation. I played through the entire game a second time and had just as much fun as the first playthrough simply because the combat is a joy to engage with. 

Everything in this game comes together into a coherent whole: rewarding exploration, light puzzles and platforming, dynamic combat, and a well developed atmosphere. I cannot recommend it enough!

It is a great game! It shows that the devs made it with love.

The game showcases your typical souls gameplay but not the difficulty(atleast later in the game). It also takes inspiration from different games in terms of gameplay, system and many more (e.g. Hollow Knight, SoTN), but the main inspiration is specifically BLOODBORNE. The lore, the setting, the NPCs, boss fights, and weapons(there's even the famous serrated weapon).

Could easily be 10/10 for me, unfortunately, the map system is really bad and the landmarks paired with metroidvania style of exploration, could easily be confusing and convoluted all the way. For now, it is easily 9.5/10 for me and could not wait for the next game in this series!

This game has SO much going for it but you can only attack in the four cardinal directions which leads to a lot of really clunky interactions. I honestly can't understand that decision in a game that already supports 360 degree inputs and movement. I ended up refunding it out of frustration.

If they ever update it to support more attack angles then I will probably pick it up again.

Tombwater is a fantastic game I have a challenging time recommending. Never before have I played a game whose reach so exceeds its grasp. The music, level design, and aesthetic are all excellent, but the moment to moment gameplay feels unpolished. This clunkiness was never enough to make me lose interest in exploring the world, and indeed it was never insurmountable, but I’d expect some people to be turned off. If you can look past the jank there’s a beautiful vision behind Tombwater that is absolutely worth your time and money.
Great game
bloodborne cowboy. The genre mashup I didnt know I needed until now.

Fun metroidvania that feels unique.

The map is extremely dense and interconnected, the devs obviously poured a lot of passion into developing this. There are multiple entries into and out of each area, allowing for a very non-linear adventure. There is a bunch of post/side game stuff that is just there for you to enjoy... or not. About 50% of this game is optional.

The combat is unique and the sheer variety of enemy designs is impressive, but you become ridiculously overpowered by late/end game if you explore everything.

The map is only a smidgen above being completely useless, this game is not for anyone who doesn't like to be lost or backtracking constantly.

Had a blast
Great music, great atmosphere, and great theme. Controls tightly and feels really good to play. A hearty recommend for this game.
Fun and well-polished

I'm leaving this review after beating the game once. I had high hopes for Tombwater and I was NOT disappointed. I thoroughly enjoyed my first playthrough, and if anything, the one criticism I would have made is that I wished it was a little harder. I say WOULD HAVE made because, shortly after finishing my playthrough, I found the options that let you tweak damage received and damage dealt! I was tremendously excited when I discovered that I could do even more challenging playthroughs. A lot has been made about soulslike games needing a difficulty option, and I've always been of the opinion that it's true - we should have the option to make the games even harder. Well here they've done it. You can also make it easier, if you're into that. If one of the devs reads this, my only request is that you let us make it harder still. Thank you.
Topdown Bloodborne in a western setting - what's not to love? :D

Combat is fun, exploration feel decent and the world building is neat, fun genre, my biggest gripe is the atrocity they’ve called a ‘map’
When I need a 3rd party map for collectibles? Good
When I need a 3rd party map just to figure out where I even am? Not good

This is the latter
Input delay, control mapping bugs, incredibly confusing navigation as levels don't really have good landmarks to identify locations relative to one another. Art and music are very nice though.

I would recommend this game so freaking hard if it wasn't one of the worst level designs i've seen in my 32 years of life. This is just unacceptable in this day and age. getting lost in exploration and trying to find the right path is one thing, but in this game every single thing looks the same and there's no real way to tell where you are in relation to your goals. the map is useless and i have never in my life found anything more boring than wandering aimlessly through this town that was unable to convey height anywhere in a town full of buildings. idk what's a roof, what's stairs, what's building i can walk behind, its all just a mess. i love the gameplay but the world is so uninspired that i couldn't be bothered to play it for even a full hour.

A beautiful 2D Pixel Soulslike in a Western Setting. The Combat is well crafted, punishing if you make mistakes but very rewarding when you get the hang of it. Exploration is a big part of the game and there is always something to find. Only negative is that sometimes it doesn't guide enough about where to go next, but that happened not too often and there is a helpful and spoiler-free guide by the devs. Definitely recommend.

Tombwater is a flawed gem of a game and is almost exactly the game I’ve been wanting for years for. A wild west souls-like with eldritch horror themes, Tombstone is a really fun game. I wasn’t really expecting as much as the game was ready to provide.

Combat:
The game’s combat is really fun, mixing melee and gunfights and dynamite. Ammo for your guns come back when you engage with melee, and things like potions and dynamite refill at bonfires. The start of the game felt somewhat easy, but definitely got more difficult as the game went on (disclaimer, I refuse to upgrade health in games like these, so that may have played a roll.). What surprised me the most was the shear number of weapons you can find in the game. I expected to just use an upgradeable sword and revolver, but by the end I was switching between a lamppost and shovel, while sniping with a rifle. The boss designs are also really creative at times. My favorites are still the piano and the electric bandit, to leave it vague.

Exploration:
Another thing that surprised me was definitely the size and scope of the world. There are multiple sizable regions in the world with a great deal of secrets to find. About the only wild west trope I DIDN’T see was a swamp land or civil war battle field, otherwise, the game covers the whole gambit. I actually had a lot of fun mapping places out on some paper, cause I was curious what it would look like; it is an absolute beautiful maze with the kind of interconnecting parts you’d see in older souls games. Locations were also varied a great deal; from old west towns to cathedrals to deserts and canyons to factories. The only thing I was disappointed in was that the traveling circus was so short. I was hoping the tents would had a Tardis like effect and I’d end up fighting a eldritch clown or something.

Bugs:
As much as I love the game, it IS somewhat buggy at times. More than once I’ve found myself unable to do anything but move, cause I think I took fatal damage while healing. So I could move around, but couldn’t attack or dodge or use items. I only got out of it once, and I don’t know what I did.
I also somehow died while the final cutscene was playing, so I had to beat the final boss twice.
Honestly though, I could just be unlucky. I tend to trigger bugs involving dying while triggering an event often in games. I don’t know why.

Conclusion:
I had so much fun playing this game that I’m eagerly hoping for a sequel. If you like souls-likes or the wild west, I would highly recommend getting a copy of this game to try out.
The only thing I hope is in the next game is that I can either play as a cowgirl or things are at least left more ambiguous, like I thought it would at first (the main character is barely detailed and reminded me of Frisk from Undertale).

Es scheint mir für die von den Entwicklern verfügbaren Mitteln ein sehr gutes Spiel zu sein. Ich habe es einmal durchgespielt und finde es wirklich klasse. Vielleicht spiele ich es ein weiters mal durch. Es scheint mehrere Endings zu geben und das Gameplay ist klasse. Die Auswahl an Waffen und Zaubern sind ausreichend und die Atmosphäre kommt gut rüber. Die Story ist Kryptisch erzählt und hält einen bei Laune.

Einzige grosse Kritikpunkte sind die wirklich fehlende Map. Es ist wirklich (nervig) mühsam sich in der Welt zurechtzufinden. Normalerweise habe ich weniger Probleme ein Spiel ohne vernünftige Karte zu spielen aber bei dieser Welt hat es mich teilweise schon sehr genervt. 
Ein weiterer kritikpunkt sind die unnötigen Werte der Starterklassen. Ausser Lucidity, Endurance und Vita braucht man eigentlich nichts (und man kann auch nichts anderes Leveln).

Alles in allem aber ein sehr solides Game welches ich nur empfehlen kann. Ich schätze mit reichlich Budget und etwas mehr Zeit (Gerade was Map und Werte der Starterklassen angeht) hätte man daraus ein weitaus besseres Game machen können. 

Dennoch. Daumen hoch. Es hat wirklich sehr viel Spass gemacht!!!

DARK SOULS: PREPARE TO GET LOST EDITION

Play this if you like Souls games for exploration (e.g. DS1, BB, Wuchang). It’s an enormous multi-layered map with tons of optional content. The in-game map does not hold your hand for better or for worse…
I enjoy the challenge and the theme. Very cool stuff and I hope there is a sequel!
western game
Good

I really do like the game. The gameplay is great, the design is awesome, and I love the "Zelda-like" dungeons aspect. It's difficult but you can mess with the settings a tad to make more your speed. The only complaint I have is this mapping system. Goal markers are virtually non existent and the map itself is so vague that you really can't make heads or tails of it. The only thing the map conveys is that you are in the general vicinity. If I had to make a suggestion, then maybe placing better landmarks or goal markers. Tombwater is a well crafted game with immaculate Lovecraftian western vibes. I've finished a complete playthrough and already miss the world and gameplay.

Some highlights:
- spooky and tightly unfolded mysteries/lore, excellent pacing 
- quirky and imaginative horror, I loved the tone throughout 
- thoughtful, layered game design where you can return to zones and keep unlocking or finding new areas and puzzles
- rich immersive areas that capture historical and beautiful environments 
- lots of choices for interesting combat,  skills you might initially overlook become OP and super satisfying to use in the right instances 
- game is generous in dropping cool and interesting items

A few peeves:
- controller controls a bit clunky (e.g. you can only aim up/down/left/right for spells and certain tools, you need to tweak the controls to make aiming with a gun bearable)
- map is pretty sparse and game does not hold your hand with tasks. Gameplay involves a bit of unnecessary backtracking because of this
- normal monster ai is a bit dumb and can lead to unintentional (and sometimes hilarious) cheesing

These peeves don't really affect the excellent gameplay and atmosphere of the game though, highly recommend!

Tombwater is a fun souls-like with some light classic Zelda-mechanics. Set in a small western town, you play as a silent protagonist, called by your former gang boss to visit him in Tombwater, a mining town were he has made the position of sheriff. Arriving there it becomes clear that some sort of supernatural horror has changed the townfolk, and you search for your former boss to find out and stop what happend.
Story wise it feels well written and the game does not drown you in overly long dialogue. Additionally, items give more lore, if you care to read. The narrative is enjoable, even if it doesn't really surprise you. You get a souls like western with eldrich elements, and it is what you expect (but still well made). 
The western setting is the big standout here, since we don't get that many of these at all, even more so with this type of horror and souls-like gameplay. And it is a great mix, the devs give you the exypected locations of towns, mines and canyons and also add some more unique locations, which still very much fit the setting. Level- and worlddesign are definitely the highlights for me, it all feels well placed and logical, with shortcuts and smartly placed fast travel points. Some levels feel a bit too maze-like, especially the first area with its many closed paths, but overall it is really fun exploring. Finding hidden weapons, bosses and characters is really enjoyable and rewarding.
Gameplay is simple and solid. Dodging is your main defensive option, while you attack with melee  weapons, fire your guns and use items like granades and different spells. Bullets replenish by attacking or by resting at savepoints. Combat-items need to be crafted, but once you made something, they get refilled everytime you rest, so there is no reason to not use them. You can also dissmalte them, giving you back all the ressources, which I really like, since it gives you a good reason to switch up your loadout and experiment.
Spells are equiped just like bombs and other offensive items. They technically have no limit in useage, but every spell cast fills your madness-meter, which slowly goes down by not using magic. If you do fill the meter, you can not use magic until you rest or die. Additionally, sometimes enemies appear, which can get quite stressfull if that happens during a big fight. The madness-meter, life and stamina can be upgreaded with skill points, which you get by simply killing enemies. Apart from these three stats, there are items to be found which upgrade you overall damage, while other items give your healing flasks more uses and regeneration. You can also equip Charms, which enhance your character with different perks, from more damage to regenerating your life by attacking enemies. It is a good mix of combat and exploration rewards, making you check every corner and also fight enemies you come across while doing so.

Of course there are some aspects that I didn't like. Some hitboxes can feel to big or lingering on after the animation is done, some zones can be a bit to convoluted and samey-looking and balancing is also not great. Early one, enemies and bosses can be quite challenging, but after the midpoint or so, level ups, Charms, strong spells and items can easily make you demolish most enemies and bosses. It is satisfing, no question,  but also takes away from the tension. Of course this happens in many games, but it is still noteworthy, I think.

Overall I still realy enjoyed the game, The 20-ish hours flew by and I had multiple long, uninterrupted play sessions, it was just a lot of fun. Hopefully the game sells well, it really deserves it.

An action RPG with some souls-like elements, TOMBWATER is a top down adventure game where you explore and uncover secrets, treasures, and horrors no man was meant to know about. The game features a world surprisingly larger than what you'd expect, and feels like Western Bloodborne and Link to the Past had a child.

The gameplay itself is tight. Buttons are responsive, and the controls don't require a whole lotta learning to get in and start playing. Combat feels good - oftentimes you'll encounter a new enemy and have a chance to learn what it does, then experience encounters where you'll have to deal with multiple foes, or patterns that compliment one another. You have your typical dash that grants you i-frames, and most enemies can be dashed through during their attacks. Stamina and Stagger work together pretty well, you get your stamina back quick and you can learn how many hits a certain attack will take to stagger a foe, giving you an opportunity to interrupt their attack to land another few hits in or use it as a window to recover.

Like most souls games, you'll have yourself a flask to get health back. The game gives you a wide plethora of ways to get health back outside of that, and towards the end of the game you can feel comfortable enough to not have to drink as often, sometimes even just not using the healing flask at all when you've mastered avoiding enemy hits. That's not to say this is an easy game, not at all - oftentimes the damage comes fast and hard, if you let yourself get struck in quick succession you'll find yourself licking the floor faster than someone saying "draw," but with patience and observation you can quickly find how to avoid those hits and how to deal with the minor scrapes you'll take along the way.

TOMBWATER offers a lot of content. The map is surprisingly huge, and you'll find yourself coming across new areas for a good while. Some of the tools you gain in this game give a Metroidvania aspect to the game, and with some clever exploration and tool usage you can actually take the game in a myriad of ways. It's pretty non-linear, and because of all the secrets in it you're highly encouraged to explore to gain as many weapons, trinkets, doodads and gizmos as you can stuff in your pockets.

Character builds offer a variety of ways to play the game. There are many weapons, most of them feel different in how they attack, or what they can bring to the field. You can have three primaries and three ranged weapons on at a time, letting you set yourself up to handle multiple situations. In addition, you'll have access to some Occult magic, with many separate sub-schools of them. Levelling up is straightforward, and you never really feel like you "built wrong" because most of the build involves your loadouts themselves. For those familiar with Hollow Knight, the game uses a system where you equip various badges that require charm slot points, each providing some kind of benefit that usually helps you further define how you want to play the game.

The game feels nice, the graphics and snappiness of things reminds me of SNES era games. Nothing's too saturated or bright, but there's a lot of effort put into the world design. The atmosphere that this game has in its audio and environment though is superb. Definitely worth taking some time to just breathe in the game, each zone feels different and has its own mood, and there are many spots in the game that drive home unexpected feelings of tension, mystery, and awe. There are some, probably unintentionally, memorable folk you'll come across. I certainly hope that there's content added later on that gives a little more story about these people.

The story itself is pretty good. It fits what it's set out to do, and it's entertaining. It leaves you wondering about things, and it does a really good job of introducing mysteries and then letting you find out the answers to them in-game. Again, exploration is highly encouraged - take your time in this one, it's worth going slow.

If I had to knock anything on this game, it's that sometimes you can notice enemies having a little trouble on obstacles. Not to say that's necessarily a bad thing, it gives you as the player a chance to take things a little easier if you want, but there are times where I would have expected an enemy to be able to go somewhere, or use A* pathfinding to get to where I'm at.

The developers are pretty good about taking feedback and bugfinding, if you encounter problems, need help figuring out something or just have general purpose conversational curiosity their discord is a good place to visit - they answer fairly fast and seem to really enjoy trying to make the game as polished as possible.

Overall, this game's great. Worth your time, worth a buy. It isn't a super sweatcore "git gud" game, but it's not baby mode either. If you like westerns, mysteries, horror, and action give this one a go for sure.

Really enjoyed my time with Tombwater.

For the record, I don't really like Legend of Zelda, and going in I was afraid of this playing too much like *A Link to the Past*. But that fear was completely unfounded.  This game plays much closer to the gameplay of *Bastion* and the exploratory elements of *Hollow Knight*. Filling in the map of Tombwater and the geography surrounding it was immensely satisfying, and did a great job establishing a scale and reality of the bombed out community we're exploring.

I've always loved the old west, and Tombwater is the most immersive exploration of an old-west-style boomtown I have ever experienced. The writing in particular deserves praise. Unlike your other attempts such as RDR, which pay lip service to the balance of money, power, regret, religion, and redemption, Tombwater focuses on a single community. Instead of overwrought exposition, the game communicates it's tension through player-directed dialogue, and visual story-telling. 

My main criticism of this game is that it's merely excellent. While Tombwater is masterful in it's application of technique, and it's story and characters are interesting and memorable, but it doesn't have the sort of innovation necessary to earn a spot in Gaming canon. 

That being said, this is a great game. If you loved Hollow Knight/Silksong, and/or thought that *The Good, The Bad, And The Ugly* was too short, you would love this game too. I bought it at $17.99 and it was worth every penny.

A solid blend of zelda and the souls games. 

The strongest part of the game is the exploration and level design. It's super interconnected, and you can really do a lot of stuff out of order if you want to. I always felt like I had somewhere to go. 

The combat is decent, although the consumable bombs are way too OP. I was able to beat a boss without moving once. 

I'm a big lovecraft fan, so I found the story and art to be pretty cool, albeit a bit predictable. It does at times feel a little too close to bloodbourne. I do know this was originally a bloodbourne demake, so I understand. The wild west setting is pretty cool though. 

Also, I should note that despite it being an indie game that only takes about ~10 hours to beat, there is a TON of content. Weapons, spells, upgrades, secret bosses, etc. I know I'm missing a bunch of stuff going off of the trailer. I'm not entirely sure, but I got a few key items that hinted at a second ending.
